newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MACLEAN WILL NOT BE PUNISHED FOR SLASHING INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MACLEAN WILL NOT BE PUNISHED FOR SLASHING INCIDENT.

text.p: No film, no foul was the ruling by the National Hockey League Saturday in the John MacLean slashing incident.
The NHL said it will not penalise the New Jersey Devils forward for slashing the New York Rangers' Niklas Sundstrom, breaking his left forearm and knocking him out of the playoffs.
The league said the incident in an Eastern Conference semifinal game on Thursday night was not seen by on-ice officials and there was no adequate videotape that would allow for a review.
Sundstrom, who had five assists in nine playoff games, was injured late in the third period when he absorbed a two-handed slash by MacLean. No penalty was assessed on the play.
The game, a 3-0 victory over the Devils that gave the Rangers a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series, was already out of New Jersey's reach when the incident occurred.

The Rangers had been hoping for disciplinary action by NHL senior vice president of hockey operations Brian Burke, who let a cross-check to the face of New Jersey's Doug Gilmour by the Rangers' Mark Messier in Game 2 go unpunished. Gilmour was not injured on the play.

Burke explained in a statement: "The League has a long-standing policy that it cannot and will not impose supplementary discipline on a player when there is not an adequate video of the incident in question and/or the incident was not seen by any of the on-ice officials."
The series resumes on Sunday afternoon in New Jersey.
